description: Declarative semantic rules evaluated by compute_verdict.py. Each rule fires when its `check` matches the observations object. The verdict is escalated to the rule's `verdict` level. Add a rule here when a previous run let a structurally-detectable failure slip past the inspector.

rules.description: Agent transcript file exists but contains fewer than MIN_TRANSCRIPT_LINES lines, meaning Channel A (content audit by grepping the transcript) is structurally blind. Most often caused by a post-summary collapse (only the bootstrap user message survived). When this happens the inspector must BLOCK rather than silently mark every Channel-A check as 'unverified', which is what hid the 2026-04-21 Qwen3 violations.
rules.remediation: Re-run the phase in a fresh agent context, OR increase MIN_TRANSCRIPT_LINES via env if the workflow legitimately has near-empty transcripts. NEVER paper this over by treating Channel A checks as unverified.

rules.description: Phase claimed kernel-opt is finished, but $RESULT_DIR/kernel_results.json still has integration_status == 'NOT_INTEGRATED'. Iron Rule IR-3 says integration is MANDATORY after every successful kernel-opt round. Skipping integration means GEAK / Claude / Codex results are never validated end-to-end.
rules.remediation: Run actions/integrate.md for every optimized kernel returned by kernel-opt: patch the kernel into the framework, re-baseline with run_baseline.sh, run the accuracy probe, then update integration_status.

rules.description: By the time SWEEP starts, every action in $RESULT_DIR/action_stack.json::dfs_order should have been attempted (success / discard / deferred-with-reason). When dfs_order is strictly longer than completed_actions, actions were silently dropped. The 2026-04-21 Qwen3 run lost 4 server-param actions this way.
rules.remediation: For each action in dfs_order missing from completed_actions: either execute it now and append to completed_actions, or move it to deferred_actions with a one-line justification. Then re-emit action_stack.json.

rules.description: BASELINE step 5 of actions/baseline.md is mandatory: it produces $RESULT_DIR/accuracy_reference.json which acts as the accuracy floor for every later DFS_LOOP and SWEEP comparison. If it is missing, every downstream accuracy claim is unfalsifiable.
rules.remediation: Run actions/baseline.md step 5 (GSM8K eval) and write the resulting score to $RESULT_DIR/accuracy_reference.json. All subsequent DFS_LOOP / SWEEP results must compare against this file.

rules.description: An Iron-Rule-derived MUST tool_call has count == 0 in a transcript that is otherwise healthy (>= MIN_TRANSCRIPT_LINES). This means the rule was not just unverifiable — it was actively skipped. Iron Rule violations escalate to FATAL per remediation-protocol.md.
rules.expected: every IR-N MUST tool_call has count >= 1
rules.remediation: Identify the IR-N rule whose tool was never called, perform the missing tool call now, and document in $RESULT_DIR/state.json why it was missed. If the rule does not apply to this phase, narrow its applies_to_phases in scripts/parse_iron_rules.py before the next run.
